entries.notes: Approved for Phase 1 commercial use. Effective license of the pinned static build 7.0.2-static (see .ffmpeg-version, MD5 7fa72b652e19bf84c9461e332ea1cdf3), configured with --enable-gpl --enable-version3 plus a full-featured --enable-lib* set including libx264, libx265, libass, libvidstab, libaom, libdav1d, libvpx, libopus, libwebp and others (see docs/component-governance.md for the full verified configuration string from `ffmpeg -version`), is GPL-2.0-or-later (the LGPL-2.1 core source becomes GPL-2.0+ once --enable-gpl pulls in GPL-licensed components such as libx264, libx265, libvidstab, libass). Determination authority: operator self-determination per FSF GPL FAQ citations; no outside counsel engaged. GPL-boundary holding: FfmpegMediaAssemblerAdapter invokes FFmpeg strictly as an external subprocess via child_process.spawn with no static/dynamic linking into Node.js, no C/C++ native addons, and communication via stdin/stdout pipes only. Per FSF GPL FAQ 'Mere Aggregation' and 'PipeLinking' clauses (URLs in licenseSource), subprocess + pipe invocation of a separately-distributed GPL program does not create a derivative work in the calling program, so the surrounding proprietary Node.js code is not contaminated by FFmpeg's GPL license. Distribution model: host-installed static binary on a separate medium from the Node.js application (downloaded and pinned via scripts/install-ffmpeg.sh; not bundled into the application's distribution archive). x264/x265 patent exposure (MPEG-LA H.264/HEVC royalties): not a concern for the current deployment jurisdiction and use case. This determination was originally made against runtime build n8.0.1 and is explicitly extended to cover the now-pinned 7.0.2-static build, which the GPL-boundary holding above applies to identically since the subprocess invocation architecture is unchanged and the additional enabled components (libx265, libvidstab, libaom, libdav1d, etc.) are also GPL/LGPL/BSD-licensed and carry no different boundary implications. Pinned runtime build continues to be evaluated at startup by apps/render-worker/src/cli/run-delivery-assembler.ts via FfmpegMediaAssemblerAdapter.getRuntimeComponents().

entries.notes: Approved for Phase 1 commercial voiceover generation. Subscription tier: Azure Pay-as-you-go / Standard (governed by Microsoft's Product Terms; commercial use permitted). Voice family: Azure Standard (pre-built) Neural voices (e.g., en-US-JennyNeural, en-US-GuyNeural). Per the Code of Conduct's 'Azure Speech and voice services in Foundry Tools' section, the special end-user voice-consent, opt-out, and voice-model-training-data (VMTD) obligations apply specifically to applications that let External Users submit their own voice for model training/personalization ('Voice Features', i.e. Personal Voice / Custom Neural Voice scenarios) — this deployment uses only pre-built Standard Neural voices with no end-user voice training, so those obligations do not apply. Determination authority: operator self-determination per the published Microsoft terms cited above; no outside counsel engaged. Volume: bounded by the deployment's Pay-as-you-go metering; no separate volume commitment required for Phase 1. Provider invocations are gated by EnforceLicenseRouting via the AssemblySpec.voiceover.source.providerId lookup in apps/application/src/use-cases/assemble-delivery-reel.ts.

entries.licenseSource: https://github.com/OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl/blob/v1.8.0/COPYING (upstream COPYING file, accessed 2026-09-07); https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html#MereAggregation (FSF GPL FAQ Mere Aggregation); https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-faq.html#PipeLinking (FSF GPL FAQ Pipe/Socket invocation)
entries.notes: Approved as a second self-hosted voice-synthesis option (issue #161), alongside the existing Kokoro option. Piper (OHF-Voice/piper1-gpl, tag v1.8.0) is licensed GPL-3.0, confirmed via the upstream COPYING file (blob sha 10926e87f113fb026c366866d6fa466061562870, identical at the v1.8.0 tag and the main branch as of 2026-09-07). Determination authority: operator self-determination per FSF GPL FAQ citations, the same standard already applied to ffmpeg and minio in this registry; no outside counsel engaged. GPL-boundary holding: deployed strictly as a standalone, unmodified upstream network service (python3 -m piper.http_server -m <voice>, per upstream docs/API_HTTP.md), not as a CLI subprocess and not via Piper's Python API or C/C++ API (libpiper) — the latter two would embed/link Piper's code directly into a calling process and are explicitly not used. A calling adapter communicates only via plain HTTP: POST /synthesize with a JSON {text: ...} body, returning WAV audio bytes; no shared memory, no exchange of internal data structures, no process-level coupling. Per FSF GPL FAQ 'Mere Aggregation' and 'PipeLinking' clauses (URLs in licenseSource), which cover pipe/socket/network communication between separate programs (subject to the caveat that sufficiently 'intimate' data exchange could combine the programs — not applicable here given the plain JSON/WAV wire protocol), this boundary does not create a derivative work in the calling application; the surrounding proprietary Node.js/TypeScript code is not contaminated by Piper's GPL-3.0 license. This mirrors the minio/AGPL-3.0 standalone-network-service precedent already in this registry, and is a cleaner boundary than the ffmpeg/subprocess precedent since there is no process-spawn-level coupling at all. Distribution model: standalone upstream service process, never embedded or bundled into the application's own distribution artifacts. Clients receive synthesized audio output only, never Piper's source code, so GPL-3.0's copyleft does not reach delivered client assets. Not yet wired into EnforceLicenseRouting pending the adapter build in issue #162; this entry unblocks that work.
